problem.text: Which bipartite graphs have the step Sidorenko property, and whether all edge-transitive bipartite graphs are weakly norming (Hatami).

claims.text: Theorems 1 and 3 give positive-semidefiniteness tests whose failure excludes the step Sidorenko property; Corollary 2 and 6: toroidal grids other than hypercubes lack it, so edge-transitive bipartite graphs need not be weakly norming; Corollary 4: a degree-path matrix test excludes many non-biregular graphs.

assumptions.text: Weighted blow-ups and second-order perturbations of step graphons; vertex-transitivity in Lemma 5.

methods.text: Perturb a weighted host so that the stepping operator averages the perturbation away; the quadratic term is governed by homomorphism counts with constrained neighbourhoods.

limitations.text: The step Sidorenko property is stronger than Sidorenko; the toroidal grids are Sidorenko by the Cartesian product theorems, so the paper does not produce a non-Sidorenko graph.

relevance.text: Shows that edge-transitive graphs reach beyond the norming method while (in the known cases) staying Sidorenko, which frames the edge-transitive candidate of this exploration.
